entries.definition: To obey because it is the truth — an obedient response, not bare assent; the opposite of “believe” is apeitheō, to disobey.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: personal trust in Christ, not mere assent — the instrument that receives salvation.
entries.citations: (John 3:36; Rom 10:16) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: Faithfulness — obedience held steady by hope in the promise; “faith without works is dead”.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: confident trust in God and His promises — the sole instrument of justification.
entries.citations: (Hab 2:4; Jas 2:17) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: Covenant relationship proven by obedience — the intimate “knew” of marriage; a stranger is one not known.
entries.citations: (Gen 4:1; Hos 4:6; Matt 7:23; 1 John 2:3-4) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6

entries.definition: Keeping the commandments — “this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments”.
entries.common_view: Commonly taught: an emotion — affection, unconditional benevolence — with the commandments optional to it.
entries.citations: (John 14:15; 1 John 5:3; 2 John 4-6) · see Love, Knowing, Faith & Belief, ch. 6
